chain.title: Break Glass, Keep Something
chain.desc: Glass no longer vanishes when you break it: Quark overwrites minecraft:loot_tables/blocks/glass.json so it drops a Glass Shard. Four shards remake a pane and the sixteen stained colours each have their own shard. MODULE FLAG: glass_shard.

chain.title: Three Rope Per String
chain.desc: Three string in a column. Rope extends downward as you place it, pulls back up, and carries mobs and blocks with it - one of Quark's oldest and least replaceable tools. MODULE FLAG: rope.

chain.title: The End Rod's Cheap Cousin
chain.desc: Iron ingots in a column. If the iron_rod_pre_end flag is on it costs iron alone; otherwise the recipe wants a vanilla end rod as well, which is a deliberate pre-End versus post-End gate. MODULE FLAGS: iron_rod, iron_rod_pre_end.

chain.title: Sixteen Bars of Gold
chain.desc: Six gold ingots laid like iron bars. Gold Bars are the only decorative metal grille Quark adds and they cost exactly what vanilla iron bars do. MODULE FLAG: gold_bars.

chain.title: A Ladder That Is Not Wood
chain.desc: Iron ingots and nuggets, three per craft. Quark also adds a ladder in every wood, but the iron one is the only one that is not a straight recolour. MODULE FLAG: iron_ladder.

chain.title: Walk Over Water
chain.desc: Iron bars in a square. Items and water fall through a Grate while players walk across it, which makes it the cheapest drop-chute floor in the game. MODULE FLAG: grate.

chain.title: Six Pipes Per Craft
chain.desc: Copper ingots around glass. Pipes push items along without redstone, and crafting one with glass gives an Encased Pipe that hides its contents - the craft reverses. MODULE FLAGS: pipes, encased_pipes.

chain.title: Under the Hopper
chain.desc: Planks and a wooden rod. The Chute drops items out of its underside into whatever is below, which is the half of a hopper that vanilla never separated out. MODULE FLAG: chute.

chain.title: Storage Without Slots
chain.desc: Planks, a wooden chest and iron. A Crate holds a large amount of a small number of item types and cannot be opened by a hopper the way a chest can. MODULE FLAG: crate.

chain.title: Redstone Builds It For You
chain.desc: A crafting table on a dropper with iron and redstone. Quark's Crafter holds a recipe and produces it on a redstone pulse - autocrafting with no tech mod involved. MODULE FLAG: crafter.

chain.title: A Coin Flip in Redstone
chain.desc: Prismarine crystals, a redstone torch and stone. It sends its signal left or right at random, which is the one logic gate vanilla redstone genuinely lacks. MODULE FLAG: redstone_randomizer.

chain.title: It Knows You Looked
chain.desc: An eye of ender on obsidian with redstone. The Ender Watcher emits a signal while a player is looking directly at it. MODULE FLAG: ender_watcher.

chain.title: Sand That Falls Upward
chain.desc: Ender pearls and colourless sand, eight at a time. Gravisand reverses its own gravity on a redstone signal. MODULE FLAG: gravisand.

chain.title: Let the Animals Eat Themselves
chain.desc: Planks around wheat. Animals breed off a stocked trough without you standing there clicking, which quietly rewrites how a farm is laid out. MODULE FLAG: feeding_trough.

chain.title: Place a Random Block
chain.desc: Iron and a wooden rod. The Trowel places a random block from your hotbar, which is the fastest way to lay a naturally mottled wall. MODULE FLAG: trowel.

chain.title: One Slot, One Crop
chain.desc: Leather and string around anything in the quark:seed_pouch_holdable tag. The pouch stacks a huge quantity of one seed and plants from it directly. MODULE FLAG: seed_pouch.

chain.title: Count the Blocks
chain.desc: Iron, a wooden rod and planks. The Abacus measures distance in the world and reads it back on 49 predicate models, one per count. MODULE FLAG: abacus.

chain.title: Pull the Metal
chain.desc: Iron, cobblestone, redstone and blue dye. With the magnet_pre_end flag it takes copper instead of a chorus fruit, so like the iron rod it has a deliberate before-and-after-the-End version. It drags metal blocks around and creates Magnetized Blocks. MODULE FLAGS: magnets, magnet_pre_end.

chain.title: A Frame You Cannot See
chain.desc: An item frame between glass panes, two at a time. The frame itself is invisible; a glow ink sac upgrades it to the glowing version. MODULE FLAG: glass_item_frame.

chain.title: Blaze Rods, Boxed
chain.desc: Blaze powder around a blaze rod. It is a light source and a fuel block in one. MODULE FLAG: blaze_lantern.

chain.title: Cut It Out of a Stoneling
chain.desc: Not a recipe: the Heart of Diamond drops from Quark's Stoneling mob (loot_tables/entities/stoneling.json). It is the gate item for both the Pickarang and the Tiny Potato, and both have a no-heart fallback recipe behind their own flag. MODULE FLAG: stonelings.

chain.title: A Pickaxe You Throw
chain.desc: A heart of diamond with diamonds and planks - or, with the pickarang_never_uses_heart flag on, diamonds and planks alone. It mines at range and comes back. MODULE FLAGS: pickarang, pickarang_never_uses_heart, stonelings.

chain.title: Netherite on the Boomerang
chain.desc: The only smithing recipe in the mod and the only unflagged one: a Pickarang, a netherite upgrade template and a netherite ingot. The Flamerang sets what it hits on fire and is the mod's genuine top tier.

chain.title: Skin the Ravager
chain.desc: Ravager Hide is a mob drop with no recipe of its own; nine compress into a Bonded Ravager Hide and back. It is the expensive half of the Backpack recipe, which also has a no-hide fallback. MODULE FLAGS: ravager_hide, backpack.

chain.title: Wear Your Chest
chain.desc: A wooden chest, iron, leather and ravager hide. The Backpack occupies the chestplate slot and adds a second row of inventory. MODULE FLAG: backpack.

chain.title: What the Wraith Leaves
chain.desc: Dropped by Quark's Wraith (loot_tables/entities/wraith.json). No recipe, no other source - a pure mob-hunt item.

chain.title: Crabs Have Legs
chain.desc: Dropped by Quark's Crab. Smelting, smoking or campfire-cooking it gives a Cooked Crab Leg, and those three are the only recipes in the whole jar with no module flag on them at all.

chain.title: Do Not Mine This
chain.desc: Found underground with its own loot table at loot_tables/misc/monster_box.json. Breaking it releases everything inside, which is the point.

chain.title: Crystals in the Cave
chain.desc: Corundum grows underground in eight colours as clusters you mine. The cluster crafts into the Corundum block, which waxes, and the coloured Rainbow Lamps are built from it. MODULE FLAGS: corundum, rainbow_lamps, rainbow_lamp_corundum.

chain.title: The Stone of the End
chain.desc: Myalite generates in the End, drops Myalite Crystal, and darkens into Dusky Myalite. Jasper, Shale, Limestone and Permafrost are its four overworld counterparts, each a mined stone with its own polished and brick ladder. MODULE FLAGS: myalite, jasper, shale, limestone, permafrost.

chain.title: Green Glazed Blocks
chain.desc: Midori is one of a dozen small building-block families - alongside duskbound blocks, blue nether bricks, netherrack bricks, blackstone bricks, dirt bricks, thatch, sturdy stone and the shingles - each behind its own module flag and each a self-contained set. MODULE FLAG: midori.

chain.title: Nine Charcoal, One Block
chain.desc: The compression blocks are Quark's simplest module family: charcoal, sticks, cactus, sugar cane, chorus fruit, bonded leather and rabbit hide, six crates and five sacks, each one flag and one reversible recipe. MODULE FLAG: charcoal_block.

notes: QUARK IS 124 SEPARATELY TOGGLEABLE FEATURES, NOT ONE MOD, AND EVERY CHAIN STEP ABOVE CARRIES ITS FLAG SO A DISABLED MODULE IS VISIBLE BEFORE THE QUEST IS WRITTEN. Verified against Quark-4.0-462.jar as shipped in this pack (Forge, MC 1.20.1; the jar also requires Zeta, which this pack ships as Zeta-1.0-31.jar). ID DETECTION AND WIDENING: 996 item models, 809 blockstates, 914 lang block./item. keys; models INTERSECT lang = 837, and that is the count used. WIDENING REJECTED for the 42 blockstate-only stems, which are 6 wall_sign / wall_hanging_sign states for the three new woods and 36 potted_* flower-pot states - none is an item. NARROWED for the 159 model-only stems, and this is the case where the naive model set OVER-counts badly: 50 of them are the abacus_0 through abacus_48 plus abacus_unset predicate models of a single item, 32 are <colour>_frame_empty / _frame_map predicate models of the dyed item frames, 13 are tropical_fish_bucket_* variant models, and the rest are backpack_locked, slime_in_a_bucket_excited, the axolotl and crab bucket colours, three lootr_* chest boats and the vanilla-slab overrides Quark ships for its vertical-slab module. NARROWED for the 43 lang-only keys: 15 are biome_map.* sub-keys of one item, 9 are music_disc_*.desc descriptions, 10 are <colour>_corundum_lamp names, and - a nice trap - block.quark.oak_ladder ('Oak Ladder'), block.quark.oak_bookshelf ('Oak Bookshelf'), block.quark.iron_chain ('Iron Chain') and block.quark.weather_sensor ('Weather Detector') are Quark RENAMING VANILLA BLOCKS, not registering new ones. THE FLAG SYSTEM - THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING FOR QUEST SAFETY: 1558 of the jar's 1564 recipe files are wrapped in a forge condition of type quark:flag naming the feature that owns them, across 124 distinct flags. Disable a module in the Quark config and its recipes disappear from the game, so any quest targeting an item behind a disabled flag is uncompletable. The six unflagged recipes are three cooked_crab_leg variants (smelting, smoking, campfire), flamerang_smithing.json, trowel_to_iron_nugget.json and dye_item.json. FLAG COUNTS THAT MATTER: vertical_slabs owns 422 recipes and 188 quark outputs on its own, shingles 186/68, stone_bricks 130/60, variant_chests 53/34, corundum 45/36, more_stone_variants 42/21, blossom_trees 36/33. Those seven flags between them account for well over half the jar and are entirely variant families. At the other end, 40-odd flags own exactly one or two recipes each and those are the mechanics that make the chain above. PAIRED PRE-END FLAGS: iron_rod/iron_rod_pre_end, magnets/magnet_pre_end, pickarang/pickarang_never_uses_heart and tiny_potato/tiny_potato_never_uses_heart each ship TWO recipes for the same item - a cheap version and a version gated behind an End-tier or Stoneling-drop ingredient - and which one is live depends on the second flag. A quest on any of those four items is safe either way, but the ingredient it asks for is not fixed. NON-RECIPE OBTAINABLE, ALL TRACED: diamond_heart and pathfinders_quill from loot_tables/entities/stoneling.json, crab_leg and crab_shell from entities/crab.json, soul_bead from entities/wraith.json, forgotten_hat from entities/forgotten.json, ancient_fruit from loot_tables/blocks/ancient_leaves.json, monster_box from loot_tables/misc/monster_box.json, clear_shard and the sixteen coloured shards by Quark overwriting minecraft's own glass loot tables, ravager_hide from ravagers, and the corundum clusters, glow shrooms, chorus twist and weeds, myalite, jasper, shale, limestone and permafrost from worldgen with block loot tables. dragon_scale and bottled_cloud have no data-side source in the jar at all - both are code-side (the dragon and the Cloud block respectively) and are therefore obtainable but not provable from datapack files, which is why neither leads a chain step. ancient_tome likewise has only an advancement and a bookshelf_books tag entry; its loot injection is code-side. DROPPED AS NOT AN OBTAINABLE ITEM: quark:matrix_enchanter. It passes every membership test - item model, lang key 'Matrix Enchanting Table', blockstate, loot table, and it is in forge:needs_diamond_tool - but data/quark/loot_tables/blocks/matrix_enchanter.json drops minecraft:enchanting_table, not itself. The Matrix Enchanting module swaps the vanilla enchanting table for this block in the world; the item never enters an inventory and no recipe produces it. MODDB: no consensus signal - moddb.json has no quark key - so ordering is the recipe graph plus flag-family size, and there is no conflict to record. DROPS BY THE DESIRABILITY RULE: every vertical_slab, shingle, stone_brick variant, variant chest, ladder, bookshelf, hollow log, leaf carpet and stool - roughly 550 of the 837 verified ids - none of which is a mechanic.
